course.benchmark_note: AP Biology depth-informed benchmark; not an AP-authorized course.
course.mapping_status: National/international benchmark synthesis. Jurisdiction-specific review is required before formal standards or credit reporting.

weeks.title: Readiness, Safety & Quantitative Biology
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do safe practices, measurement, statistics, and transparent records make biological evidence more trustworthy?
weeks.phenomenon: Two teams measure the same biological sample and report different values. Which differences are normal variation, and which suggest a design or recording problem?
weeks.lab: Safety-case analysis; measurement/graphing diagnostic; no biological culturing.
weeks.concepts: hazard vs risk; variables; controls; uncertainty; mean/range; graph choice
weeks.quantitative: Compute mean, percent change, and simple uncertainty from a supplied dataset.
weeks.reading: Course safety charter and a teacher-approved biological dataset.

weeks.title: Water, Carbon & the Chemistry of Life
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why do a few chemical properties make water and carbon so important to living systems?
weeks.phenomenon: Water climbs a paper fiber and beads on a waxed surface even though gravity acts on both.
weeks.lab: Safe capillary-action or surface-tension investigation using water only.
weeks.concepts: polarity; hydrogen bonding; cohesion; adhesion; carbon skeletons
weeks.quantitative: Compare ratios and percent composition in simple biomolecule data.
weeks.reading: Open biology text section on water, carbon, and biomolecules.

weeks.title: Macromolecules & Structure–Function
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does molecular structure constrain biological function?
weeks.phenomenon: Two foods can contain similar calories but behave very differently in water and digestion models.
weeks.lab: Food-label/data classification; paper model of monomers and polymers.
weeks.concepts: carbohydrates; lipids; proteins; nucleic acids; monomer/polymer
weeks.quantitative: Interpret nutrition/macromolecule tables without making medical claims.
weeks.reading: Teacher-approved molecular structure diagrams and food-label examples.

weeks.title: Enzymes & Reaction Rates
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do enzymes change reaction pathways without being consumed?
weeks.phenomenon: The same reaction proceeds at very different rates under different conditions.
weeks.lab: Catalase-style dataset analysis or supervised safe simulation; no ingestion.
weeks.concepts: enzyme; active site; activation energy; denaturation; rate
weeks.quantitative: Graph reaction rate against temperature or substrate concentration.
weeks.reading: Open text on enzymes and reaction-energy diagrams.

weeks.title: Cell Theory & Cellular Organization
weeks.essentialQuestion: What evidence supports the cell as the basic unit of life?
weeks.phenomenon: Microscope images from very different organisms reveal recurring structural patterns.
weeks.lab: Prepared-image analysis or supervised microscopy of prepared slides.
weeks.concepts: cell theory; prokaryote; eukaryote; membrane; cytoplasm
weeks.quantitative: Use scale bars to estimate actual cell size.
weeks.reading: Prepared micrographs from a trusted educational source.

weeks.title: Membranes, Transport & Surface Area
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why can a cell not simply grow forever?
weeks.phenomenon: Small cubes exchange material faster relative to volume than large cubes.
weeks.lab: Agar-cube simulation if supervised, or paper/computational diffusion model.
weeks.concepts: selective permeability; diffusion; osmosis; active transport; SA:V
weeks.quantitative: Calculate surface-area-to-volume ratios and percent diffusion.
weeks.reading: Open text on membrane transport and cell-size constraints.

weeks.title: Organelles, Energy Systems & Endosymbiosis
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do specialized cell structures cooperate as a system?
weeks.phenomenon: Mitochondria and chloroplasts share unusual features with bacteria.
weeks.lab: Organelle evidence matrix and model comparison; no culturing.
weeks.concepts: nucleus; ribosome; ER; Golgi; mitochondrion; chloroplast; endosymbiotic evidence
weeks.quantitative: Compare organelle abundance across specialized cell types.
weeks.reading: Trusted diagrams and evidence summaries on organelles and endosymbiosis.

weeks.title: Cell Specialization, Tissues & Systems
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can cells with the same genome become structurally and functionally different?
weeks.phenomenon: Nerve, muscle, blood, and epithelial cells share DNA but have different shapes and proteins.
weeks.lab: Image-based cell specialization classification and systems model.
weeks.concepts: differentiation; gene expression; tissue; organ; organ system
weeks.quantitative: Analyze cell-type abundance or morphology data.
weeks.reading: Open text on differentiation and hierarchical organization.

weeks.title: Photosynthesis: Capturing Energy
weeks.essentialQuestion: How is light energy transformed into chemical energy?
weeks.phenomenon: Leaves exposed to different light conditions accumulate different amounts of stored chemical energy.
weeks.lab: Leaf-disk photosynthesis only with teacher supervision, or simulation/data analysis.
weeks.concepts: chloroplast; light reactions; carbon fixation; glucose; limiting factor
weeks.quantitative: Graph photosynthetic rate vs light or CO2 data.
weeks.reading: Open text on photosynthesis and energy transformations.

weeks.title: Cellular Respiration & ATP
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do cells release usable energy from organic molecules?
weeks.phenomenon: Active tissues consume oxygen and release carbon dioxide at different rates.
weeks.lab: Respirometry simulation or germinating-seed dataset; avoid sealed living-organism experiments without supervision.
weeks.concepts: glycolysis; aerobic respiration; ATP; redox; fermentation
weeks.quantitative: Compare ATP yield models and respirometry rates.
weeks.reading: Open text on cellular respiration and ATP.

weeks.title: Matter Cycling Through Metabolism
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why is matter recycled while energy flows?
weeks.phenomenon: Carbon atoms in food can later appear in exhaled carbon dioxide or new biomass.
weeks.lab: Carbon-tracing model with cards or digital system model.
weeks.concepts: conservation of matter; metabolic pathway; biosynthesis; decomposition
weeks.quantitative: Complete atom accounting through simplified reactions.
weeks.reading: Teacher-approved carbon-tracing diagrams.

weeks.title: Experimental Energetics & Metabolic Evidence
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do scientists infer metabolic processes from indirect measurements?
weeks.phenomenon: Different organisms or tissues produce distinct gas, heat, or mass-change patterns.
weeks.lab: Analyze a supplied metabolic dataset; design a safe follow-up investigation.
weeks.concepts: rate; control; respiration proxy; confounding variable; uncertainty
weeks.quantitative: Calculate rates, normalize by mass, and compare variability.
weeks.reading: A published or teacher-prepared metabolism dataset.

weeks.title: Cell Communication
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do cells send, receive, and interpret signals?
weeks.phenomenon: The same signaling molecule can trigger different responses in different cell types.
weeks.lab: Signal-transduction card/model simulation.
weeks.concepts: receptor; ligand; transduction; response; specificity
weeks.quantitative: Interpret dose-response graphs qualitatively and quantitatively.
weeks.reading: Open text on receptors and cell signaling.

weeks.title: Feedback & Homeostasis
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do feedback loops stabilize changing biological systems?
weeks.phenomenon: Body temperature remains within a narrow range despite changing environmental conditions.
weeks.lab: Feedback-loop modeling using non-clinical sample data.
weeks.concepts: homeostasis; negative feedback; positive feedback; set range; effector
weeks.quantitative: Graph deviation and recovery in a feedback dataset.
weeks.reading: Open text on feedback; use only non-diagnostic data.

weeks.title: Cell Cycle, Mitosis & Growth
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do organisms grow while maintaining genetic continuity?
weeks.phenomenon: A developing organism increases cell number dramatically without changing chromosome count in most cells.
weeks.lab: Prepared root-tip images or mitosis image set; no chemical preparation required.
weeks.concepts: cell cycle; mitosis; cytokinesis; chromosome; checkpoint
weeks.quantitative: Calculate mitotic index from prepared images.
weeks.reading: Prepared mitosis micrographs and open text.

weeks.title: Cell-Cycle Regulation & Model Boundaries
weeks.essentialQuestion: What happens when regulatory systems fail, and what can models legitimately claim?
weeks.phenomenon: Some cell lines divide despite signals that normally stop division.
weeks.lab: Case-data analysis on cell-cycle control; explicitly non-diagnostic.
weeks.concepts: checkpoint; apoptosis; mutation; regulation; correlation
weeks.quantitative: Interpret proliferation curves and distinguish correlation from mechanism.
weeks.reading: Trusted educational overview of cell-cycle regulation.

weeks.title: Semester Synthesis Investigation
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can multiple lines of evidence support one biological explanation?
weeks.phenomenon: A biological system changes under a controlled environmental condition.
weeks.lab: Student-designed safe investigation or simulation with teacher approval.
weeks.concepts: question; model; method; data; CER; limitation
weeks.quantitative: Choose appropriate summary statistics and graph.
weeks.reading: Student-selected teacher-approved background sources.

weeks.title: Midterm Examination & Corrections
weeks.essentialQuestion: What have I mastered across cells, energy, signaling, and scientific practice?
weeks.phenomenon: A cumulative evidence set connects molecular, cellular, and organismal scales.
weeks.lab: No new wet lab; midterm, correction conference, portfolio audit.
weeks.concepts: cumulative synthesis
weeks.quantitative: Mixed data interpretation and quantitative biology.
weeks.reading: Review portfolio, models, lab notes, and vocabulary.

weeks.title: Meiosis & Sources of Variation
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does meiosis create genetic variation while reducing chromosome number?
weeks.phenomenon: Siblings from the same parents can be genetically different.
weeks.lab: Chromosome-model simulation of meiosis and recombination.
weeks.concepts: homolog; meiosis; crossing over; independent assortment; gamete
weeks.quantitative: Count possible chromosome combinations in simplified models.
weeks.reading: Open text on meiosis and variation.

weeks.title: Mendelian Inheritance
weeks.essentialQuestion: When do simple inheritance models work well, and when do they fail?
weeks.phenomenon: Some traits follow predictable ratios while others do not.
weeks.lab: Probability simulation with coins/cards; no human trait diagnosis.
weeks.concepts: allele; genotype; phenotype; dominance; segregation
weeks.quantitative: Punnett probabilities and expected ratios.
weeks.reading: Open genetics text emphasizing model limits.

weeks.title: Probability, Pedigrees & Statistical Reasoning
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why are inheritance predictions probabilistic rather than guarantees?
weeks.phenomenon: A small family can differ greatly from an expected Mendelian ratio.
weeks.lab: Anonymous/published pedigree interpretation; no family medical inference.
weeks.concepts: pedigree; probability; sample size; expected vs observed; sex-linked
weeks.quantitative: Use product/sum rules and simple chi-square conceptually.
weeks.reading: Teacher-approved fictional or historical pedigrees.

weeks.title: Complex Traits & Gene–Environment Interaction
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why can phenotype not always be predicted from one gene?
weeks.phenomenon: Identical genotypes can show different phenotypes under different conditions.
weeks.lab: Plant/organism dataset analysis or simulation.
weeks.concepts: polygenic; pleiotropy; environment; penetrance; quantitative trait
weeks.quantitative: Interpret distributions and correlations without causal overclaiming.
weeks.reading: Open text on complex traits and gene–environment interactions.

weeks.title: DNA Structure & Replication
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does molecular structure enable faithful information storage and copying?
weeks.phenomenon: DNA can be copied with high fidelity despite billions of molecular events.
weeks.lab: Paper/digital DNA replication model.
weeks.concepts: DNA; nucleotide; antiparallel; base pairing; replication
weeks.quantitative: Estimate base composition from pairing rules.
weeks.reading: Open text on DNA structure and replication.

weeks.title: Transcription, Translation & the Genetic Code
weeks.essentialQuestion: How is information in DNA converted into functional molecules?
weeks.phenomenon: A single nucleotide change can alter a protein sequence—or have no effect.
weeks.lab: Codon-table translation exercise using fictional sequences.
weeks.concepts: transcription; RNA; codon; translation; ribosome; protein
weeks.quantitative: Translate sequences and compare mutation outcomes.
weeks.reading: Open text and standard genetic-code table.

weeks.title: Gene Regulation & Epigenetic Mechanisms
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why are different genes active in different cells and conditions?
weeks.phenomenon: Cells with identical DNA produce different sets of proteins.
weeks.lab: Gene-regulation network model; no human predictive claims.
weeks.concepts: promoter; transcription factor; regulation; epigenetic mark; expression
weeks.quantitative: Interpret gene-expression heatmaps or fold-change data.
weeks.reading: Open text on gene regulation and epigenetic mechanisms.

weeks.title: Biotechnology, Genomics & Bioethics
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can biotechnology modify, measure, or interpret biological information responsibly?
weeks.phenomenon: DNA technologies can identify sequences, edit genes, or produce useful molecules.
weeks.lab: Paper gel-electrophoresis analysis, sequence comparison, and ethics case.
weeks.concepts: PCR; electrophoresis; sequencing; CRISPR concept; consent; privacy
weeks.quantitative: Estimate fragment sizes from a calibration curve.
weeks.reading: Trusted biotechnology overview; no procedural gene-editing instructions.

weeks.title: Evidence for Evolutionary Change
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do multiple independent evidence streams inform explanations of biological history?
weeks.phenomenon: Fossils, anatomy, biogeography, and DNA patterns can converge on similar relationships.
weeks.lab: Evidence-station analysis using published images/data.
weeks.concepts: fossil; homologous structure; biogeography; molecular evidence; inference
weeks.quantitative: Compare sequence differences and stratigraphic patterns.
weeks.reading: NGSS-aligned evolution evidence resources.

weeks.title: Population Genetics & Changing Allele Frequencies
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can population-level genetic composition change over generations?
weeks.phenomenon: Allele frequencies shift in a simulated population under different conditions.
weeks.lab: Allele-frequency simulation with cards/spreadsheet.
weeks.concepts: allele frequency; selection; drift; gene flow; mutation
weeks.quantitative: Calculate simple allele frequencies and changes over time.
weeks.reading: Open population-genetics introduction.

weeks.title: Natural Selection & Adaptation
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can differential survival and reproduction change populations?
weeks.phenomenon: Trait distributions change after an environmental shift.
weeks.lab: Selection simulation using paper tokens or supplied data.
weeks.concepts: variation; heritability; fitness; selection pressure; adaptation
weeks.quantitative: Compare trait-frequency distributions across generations.
weeks.reading: NGSS natural-selection evidence statements.

weeks.title: Speciation, Phylogeny & Origins Literacy
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do scientists reconstruct relationships and test historical explanations?
weeks.phenomenon: Different datasets can produce competing phylogenetic trees.
weeks.lab: Build/compare phylogenetic trees from a supplied character matrix.
weeks.concepts: speciation; reproductive isolation; phylogeny; common ancestry; model; worldview
weeks.quantitative: Score parsimony or sequence-distance examples.
weeks.reading: Scientific phylogeny text plus a respectful distinction among empirical, historical, philosophical, and theological claims.

weeks.title: Ecosystem Energy Flow
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why are food webs limited by energy transfer?
weeks.phenomenon: Biomass and organism numbers usually decline across trophic levels.
weeks.lab: Food-web and energy-pyramid dataset analysis.
weeks.concepts: producer; consumer; trophic level; productivity; efficiency
weeks.quantitative: Calculate ecological efficiency and energy transfer.
weeks.reading: Open ecology text on energy flow.

weeks.title: Biogeochemical Cycles
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does matter move among living and nonliving reservoirs?
weeks.phenomenon: A carbon atom can move among atmosphere, ocean, organism, and rock over different timescales.
weeks.lab: Carbon/nitrogen cycle systems model.
weeks.concepts: carbon cycle; nitrogen cycle; reservoir; flux; feedback
weeks.quantitative: Interpret flux diagrams and compare reservoir sizes.
weeks.reading: Open system-cycle diagrams.

weeks.title: Population & Community Dynamics
weeks.essentialQuestion: What controls population size and community change?
weeks.phenomenon: Populations can grow rapidly, stabilize, oscillate, or collapse.
weeks.lab: Population model spreadsheet or supplied long-term dataset.
weeks.concepts: exponential; logistic; carrying capacity; competition; predation; succession
weeks.quantitative: Fit/interpret growth curves and percent change.
weeks.reading: Published ecology dataset or open text.

weeks.title: Biodiversity, Resilience & Human Impacts
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can societies reduce biodiversity loss while respecting ecological and human constraints?
weeks.phenomenon: Two restoration plans have different costs, risks, and ecological benefits.
weeks.lab: Biodiversity index or restoration-design analysis; protect sensitive locations.
weeks.concepts: biodiversity; resilience; ecosystem service; fragmentation; restoration
weeks.quantitative: Compute richness/evenness or compare intervention outcomes.
weeks.reading: Trusted conservation and restoration case study.

weeks.title: Biology & Biotechnology Capstone
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can biological evidence support a responsible solution to a real problem?
weeks.phenomenon: A local or global biological problem requires tradeoffs among evidence, feasibility, ethics, and uncertainty.
weeks.lab: Design project: conservation, bioengineering, health-literacy, agriculture, or biotechnology topic; teacher-approved.
weeks.concepts: criteria; constraint; stakeholder; evidence; prototype/model; ethics
weeks.quantitative: Use at least one quantitative model and uncertainty statement.
weeks.reading: Student-selected trusted sources.

weeks.title: Comprehensive Final & Portfolio Defense
weeks.essentialQuestion: Can I integrate biological concepts and scientific practices across unfamiliar contexts?
weeks.phenomenon: A multi-part case requires molecular, cellular, genetic, evolutionary, and ecological reasoning.
weeks.lab: No new wet lab; cumulative final, corrections, and portfolio defense.
weeks.concepts: cumulative synthesis
weeks.quantitative: Mixed quantitative and data-analysis tasks.
weeks.reading: Complete course portfolio and review map.

assessment.unit: Performance task: model + data/quantitative reasoning + CER + application/design
assessment.midterm: 15-item cumulative objective check plus corrections and portfolio review
assessment.final: 30-item cumulative objective check plus portfolio/capstone defense

safety.lab_policy: Target ≥25% of instructional time in inquiry, lab, simulation-with-data, fieldwork, or supervised hands-on investigation.
safety.home_rule: Use only explicitly safe investigations; substitute simulation/data analysis whenever proper supervision or facilities are unavailable.
